claims.text: Chronic: praziquantel for 1 day (2 doses for S. haematobium, S. mansoni, S. intercalatum; 3 doses for S. japonicum, S. mekongi); it kills adult worms, not developing schistosomula or eggs, so asymptomatic travelers are treated 6-8 weeks after the last exposure.
claims.quote: Recommended treatment of chronic schistosomiasis is with 1 day of praziquantel (2 doses for S. haematobium, S. mansoni, and S. intercalatum; 3 doses for S. japonicum and S. mekongi. Praziquantel is effective against adult schistosomes, but not developing schistosomula or eggs, which are present early in infection. Thus, for travelers who have no symptoms but had exposure in potentially contaminated fresh water, treatment is delayed for 6 to 8 weeks after the last exposure.
Treatment of acute schistosomiasis (Katayama fever) is based on limited data.

claims.text: oral glucocorticoids can ease severe symptoms (low-dose prednisone for 5 days in adults is usually effective); once symptoms subside, praziquantel, repeated 4-6 weeks later.
claims.quote: Systemic (oral) glucocorticoids can ameliorate severe symptoms; treatment with low-dose prednisone daily for 5 days in adults is usually effective. Once symptoms have subsided, treatment with praziquantel is given as for chronic schistosomiasis and repeated 4 to 6 weeks later after parasites have reached adulthood.

claims.text: Praziquantel adverse effects are generally mild: abdominal pain, diarrhea, headache, dizziness.
claims.quote: Adverse effects of praziquantel are generally mild and include abdominal pain, diarrhea, headache, and dizziness.
